assumptions.summary: The present network importance is measured for the current data snapshot.
Coauthor ties are treated as undirected and a repeated citation is counted once.
Cooperation counts above the chosen threshold contribute a constant term.
Citation feedback between papers with a relation is treated as equal in the base case.
Paper influence is ordered IF > r > H for AHP.
Five-year average movie box office can proxy actor strength.

summary separates importance from influence before extending the network: Name the two indices, combine local structure with mutual influence, transfer the scheme to papers and actors, then state sensitivity and generalization boundaries.
introduction turns vague influence into factors and numbered tasks: List the observable factors for researchers and papers, then convert them into explicit data, ranking, transfer, and utility tasks.
a deletion counterexample triggers clustering information: Show that equal degree can cause different connectivity damage, then add clustering to recover neighbor structure.

local graph measures and cooperation history form a composite importance: Normalize degree-neighbor and clustering terms, add the saturated Erdos-cooperation contribution, and name the resulting index.
a descriptive importance ranking is rejected as the final influence measure: Read old and young researcher cases, explain why partner quality matters, and switch to PageRank for mutual influence.
a matrix construction hands partner importance to an eigenvector: Define importance-weighted adjacency, normalize and transpose it, then solve the dominant non-negative eigenvector.

rank movement is interpreted through the added network mechanism: Compare importance and influence ranks, isolate stable, positive, and negative cases, and connect a named movement to partner quality or sparse contact.

lack of a direct paper-quality measure triggers an indirect three-factor score: Use citation influence, first-author H-index, and journal IF, order them with AHP, check consistency, and compute a final score.
a network model transfers to movie stars with a new strength proxy: Replace the central node, define the actor relation, add five-year box office, read an exception, and disclose the sample boundary.
broad network applications are kept as bounded mappings: Map nodes, edges, and indices to institutions, cities, or social users, then require reconstruction and safeguards before operational use.
node deletion turns graph importance into a ranking-deviation test: Delete high-, middle-, and low-index nodes, recompute ranks, and relate the deviation to the removed node's importance.
citation feedback asymmetry ends in a local parameter boundary: Vary the cited-to-citing impact ratio, read the deviation curve, and retain the interval where the displayed results change less.
tables and figures are read into a reproducibility check: Quote a displayed rank, count, or curve interval, state its analytical role, and name the data, comparator, or validation needed next.
strengths are paired with concrete data and sample weaknesses before use: State the graph, PageRank, or AHP benefit, disclose data and sample limits, and bound any application to decision support.

title: Methods of Measuring Influence Using Network Model
unresolved_questions: The Erdos-1 population is restricted to 511 direct collaborators, and the inclusion/exclusion construction is not released.
The collaboration graph is treated as undirected and a repeated citation is counted once; tie strength, direction, and temporal information are lost.
The cooperation-history term saturates at x=65 without calibration, confidence interval, or sensitivity to the threshold.
PageRank matrix orientation, scaling, eigenvector normalization, dangling nodes, initialization, and convergence evidence are incomplete.
The stable/positive/negative ranking classes and named examples are descriptive comparisons without an independent influence outcome.
Only 15 papers are selected; citation, H-index, IF provenance, collection dates, and field normalization are not documented.
The AHP ordering IF>r>H is subjective even though the reported CI and CR show internal consistency.
Citation feedback is assumed equal in the base paper network despite directed citing; the adjacency and citation data are not reproducibly listed.
The movie-star test uses a Tony Leung-centered 31-actor network and a five-year average box-office proxy; selection and data provenance are narrow.
Academic, military, city, and social-network applications are hypothetical mappings and cannot justify causal intervention or target selection.
Deletion sensitivity evaluates only three selected nodes and measures rank deviation rather than value uncertainty or prediction error.
The feedback-ratio curve supports only a local u interval; no full-rank, score, or uncertainty analysis is shown.
The weaknesses admit small paper/actor samples and AHP subjectivity; the final generalization claim must preserve those limits.

vague influence -> observable factors -> four tasks -> assumptions
degree success/failure -> equal-degree deletion counterexample -> clustering repair
local degree and clustering -> normalization -> cooperation saturation -> q
